newsitem.title: GERMANY: German barley harvest slowed by rain, yields lower.
newsitem.headline: German barley harvest slowed by rain, yields lower.

text.p: Rain is slowing down Germany's barley harvest as farmers have to pause to allow the crop to dry in order to avoid quality losses, the farm union (DBV) said in a statement.

National yields varied widely but were generally believed to be below last year's 5.61 tonnes per hectare, DBV added. Yields on light soils in northern German export regions ranged from around 5.5 to 7.0 tonnes per hectare.
Harvesting in most regions has only just started.

Price were beginning to stabilise but allowed no firm clues to barley marketing opportunities by the trade in 1997/98 because early volumes tend to be stored for on-farm feeding or traded between farms.
The barley area (winter and spring) for the 1997 harvest was expanded by 7.3 percent over 1996 to 2.37 million hectares.
A DBV survey showed some 60 to 70 percent of harvesting in the marginal southwestern Baden region had been completed and good hectolitre weights were reported.
Other regions which usually harvest early were Baden-Wuerttemberg, Rhineland-Palatinate south and southern Hesse, where between 20 and 40 percent had been done.
Qualities in these regions were also good but some problems with weeds, dirt and lodging were reported in eastern German states, where early rye was also affected.
Germany last year harvested 12.07 million tonnes of barley.
